Useful adaptation notes from guidelines v2.6 and purchased examples:

1) Temporal 'since' in present perfect recency/frame contexts:
- Example: "Its been a few years since I have been to Ipanema."
- Label 'since' as p.Time / p.Time when it marks elapsed time from a past event up to reference time.

2) Genitives/possessives are highly construction-sensitive:
- "Stuart's ethical and focused strategies": possessor names an associated whole/entity for the strategies, annotated p.Gestalt / p.Gestalt.
- "our business": possessive determiner can be non-literal possession; for membership/affiliation with an organization, use p.OrgMember / p.Possessor.
- "your money": ordinary ownership is p.Possessor / p.Possessor.
- "your massive contributions": with deverbal noun contribution, possessive determiner may express the semantic subject/agent rather than ownership; here p.Agent / p.Gestalt.

3) 'of' has several common but distinct uses:
- Partitive "Each of you": item-member relation, annotate complement as p.QuantityItem / p.Whole.
- Stimulus adjective/complement pattern "proud of ...": semantic role is p.Stimulus, lexical function tends toward aboutness/topic, so p.Stimulus / p.Topic.
- With nominalizations/event-result nouns like "the rewards of this program", the 'of'-phrase can denote the causal source; here p.Force / p.Force.

4) Motion/transfer-style 'to' with human endpoint under recommend:
- "recommend this place to anyone": recipient-like addressee role with directional coding, p.Recipient / p.Goal.

5) Duration:
- "throughout the year" is p.Duration / p.Duration.

General reminders from guidelines relevant to these examples:
- Separate scene role from lexical function; possessive markers often have lexical function p.Possessor or p.Gestalt even when the scene role is something else (e.g., p.Agent, p.OrgMember).
- For genitives, distinguish ownership (p.Possessor), whole/associated entity (p.Gestalt), and semantic participant readings licensed by relational/deverbal nouns.
- For adjective complements like 'proud of', expect non-matching construals where the role is emotional trigger (p.Stimulus) but the adposition's lexical contribution is p.Topic.
- For recipient-marking 'to', lexical function frequently remains directional/endpoint-like (p.Goal) even when the scene role is p.Recipient.
